shared_elements: bearded male human figures in profile, standing
long fringed/pleated robes with patterned edges
stylised layered hair and beard rendered as rows of curls
figures carrying or holding objects (cup, whisk, staff/spear, vessels)
attendant/retainer figures following or facing a principal figure
low-relief profile heads with frontal eye convention
horizontal register/band divisions with ornamental border strip
hooved quadruped animal in profile (in B)
justification: Both depict bearded men in profile with elaborately curled hair and beards, wearing long patterned robes and carrying objects and weapons, arranged along a groundline in attendant-to-principal relationships, with rows framed by ornamental bands — a fairly specific shared repertoire rather than generic "standing figures". The clearest difference in content is scale and scheme: A is a single large panel of two figures confronting each other with cup and whisk over a field of inscription, whereas B is a long multi-register procession of many small figures leading animals and bearing tribute, with no text and no confronted pair.
